sections.title: Sound of letter oo
paragraphs: The letter (у) /u/ is named by its sound. It mainly makes the sound /u/, heard in (ухо) /ˈu.xə/, which means ear. This Russian letter makes two different sounds.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: To make the first sound, pull your tongue back. Round your lips tightly into a small circle. Push your lips forward and let your voice vibrate. For the second sound, keep your mouth slightly wider. Relax your tongue slightly. Put your hand on your neck to feel your voice buzz steadily.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: You say the sound /u/ when the letter has the stress, as in (утро) /ˈu.trə/. It also sounds like the sound /u/ before the stressed beat, as in (рука) /ruˈka/. In other unstressed positions, it makes the sound /ʊ/, like in (улица) /ˈu.lʲɪ.tsə/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not add a w sound at the end, like in English boot. Keep your lips still throughout the entire sound. Also, do not pronounce it like the vowel in book when stressed. Push your lips forward firmly to keep the sound pure.
